answer.note: The four ref files have identical text and give no file-specific guidance, so I chose C and D from the repo. A grep for volume, difficulty and bugs matched only radon/metrics.py (C), so that is where the conversion formulas and zero-count handling are. I did not open the other files. I picked D (radon/visitors.py) because I expect it to produce the operator and operand counts, but I haven't checked that. Suggested 60-minute split: metrics.py 35 min (vocabulary, volume, difficulty, effort, time and bugs formulas, and division or log of zero); visitors.py 15 min (how the counts are gathered, and whether they can be zero or double-counted); complexity.py 5 min; raw.py 5 min. The last two are likely peripheral, so skim them only for Halstead use.
